- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to capture mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Model underestimates the true mean of recent 30-day history, particularly when recent prices are trending downward.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates the depth of a fall until 10–15 days later.
- When true outcome is below 70, model tends to overpredict by 1–3 points, especially if recent history includes low values.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistently underestimates 70–72 range when recent history includes 73–75.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — e.g., after a 70–72 drop, model often forecasts a sharp rebound instead of a gradual recovery.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events — e.g., when true outcome drops below 70 after a policy change, model doesn’t adjust downward enough.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — forecasts appear “too flat” when true outcome shows sharp swings.
- Model often misjudges the “bottom” of a price correction — underestimates the true low and then overcorrects later.
